title: DSA with C++
description: Complete Data Structures and Algorithms in C++ from setup to advanced: 100 lessons, each with notes, logic and practice problems.

lessons.title: 001. Setup and First Program
lessons.notes:
Install g++ (MinGW / Xcode CLT / apt) and VS Code.
Compile: g++ main.cpp -o main
Run: ./main
Every program starts at main().

logic.problem: Print "Hello, DSA" and run it.
logic.thinking: Where does a C++ program start, and how does it become something runnable?
logic.logic: Source code is compiled by g++ into an executable.
logic.approach:
1. Write main.cpp.
2. Compile it.
3. Run the output.
logic.code:
#include <iostream>
int main() { std::cout << "Hello, DSA\n"; }

lessons.title: 002. Program Structure and Headers

logic.problem: Why does my program need #include lines?
logic.thinking: Code you did not write must be brought in before use.
logic.logic: A header declares what a library offers.
logic.approach:
1. Include the header.
2. Use its names.
3. Compile.

lessons.title: 003. Variables and Data Types
lessons.notes:
int (4 bytes, about ±2.1e9), long long (8 bytes, about ±9.2e18), double, char, bool.
Overflow: int * int can exceed the range. Use long long when values reach 1e5 * 1e5.
sizeof(type) shows the size.

logic.problem: Why does 100000 * 100000 print a wrong number?
logic.thinking: The result needs more than 32 bits.
logic.logic: Choose the type by the largest value you may store.
logic.approach:
1. Estimate the max value.
2. If above 2e9, use long long.
logic.code: long long x = 100000LL * 100000;

lessons.title: 004. Input, Output and Fast I/O

logic.problem: Read n numbers and print their sum quickly.
logic.thinking: Large inputs make slow I/O the bottleneck.
logic.logic: Untie cin from cout and skip C-stdio sync.
logic.approach:
1. Add the two lines at the top of main.
2. Read in a loop.
3. Print with "\n".

lessons.title: 005. Operators
lessons.notes:
Arithmetic + - * / %; integer division truncates.
Logical && || !; bitwise & | ^ ~ << >>
x++ vs ++x; use brackets when unsure about precedence.
= assigns, == compares.

logic.problem: Check if a number is even, or a power of two.
logic.thinking: Bit operations answer yes/no questions in O(1).
logic.logic: n & (n - 1) clears the lowest set bit.
logic.approach:
1. Even: n % 2 == 0.
2. Power of two: n > 0 and (n & (n-1)) == 0.
logic.code: bool isPow2(int n) { return n > 0 && (n & (n - 1)) == 0; }

lessons.title: 006. Conditionals
lessons.notes:
if / else if / else, switch (needs break), ternary a ? b : c.
Check the edge case first (empty, zero, negative).

logic.problem: Decide which branch handles each input.
logic.thinking: Write conditions from most specific to most general.
logic.logic: Exactly one branch should run for each input.
logic.approach:
1. List the cases.
2. Order them.
3. Test the borders.
logic.code: if (x < 0) cout << "neg"; else if (x == 0) cout << "zero"; else cout << "pos";

lessons.title: 007. Loops
lessons.notes:
for (init; cond; step), while, do-while.
break leaves the loop, continue skips to the next round.
The number of rounds decides the time complexity.

logic.problem: Check whether n is prime.
logic.thinking: Divisors come in pairs, so look only up to √n.
logic.logic: If d divides n, so does n/d.
logic.approach:
1. Loop i from 2 while i*i <= n.
2. If n % i == 0, not prime.
3. Otherwise prime.

lessons.title: 008. Pattern Printing
lessons.notes:
Outer loop = rows, inner loop = columns.
Find the rule: stars per row, spaces per row.
Dry-run n = 3 on paper first.

logic.problem: Print a right triangle of stars.
logic.thinking: Row i has i stars.
logic.logic: Rows drive the outer loop, the row rule drives the inner loop.
logic.approach:
1. for i in 1..n.
2. for j in 1..i print *.
3. Print a newline.

lessons.title: 009. Functions
lessons.notes:
Return type, name, parameters.
Default arguments and overloading.
Pass by value copies; use a reference to avoid copying big data.
Declare before use (prototype).

logic.problem: Compute power(a, b) as a reusable piece.
logic.thinking: Split the program into small testable pieces.
logic.logic: One function does one job.
logic.approach:
1. Name the job.
2. Decide inputs and output.
3. Test it alone.

lessons.title: 010. References and Pointers
lessons.notes:
int& r = x; r is another name for x.
int* p = &x; *p reads x, p holds the address.
Pass big vectors as const vector<int>&.
nullptr means "points to nothing".

logic.problem: Swap two numbers in a function.
logic.thinking: A copy cannot change the original.
logic.logic: A reference works on the caller's variable.
logic.approach:
1. Take both params by &.
2. Swap using a temp.
logic.code: void swp(int& a, int& b) { int t = a; a = b; b = t; }

lessons.title: 011. Arrays
lessons.notes:
int a[n]; index 0..n-1; no bounds checking.
Global arrays start as 0, local arrays hold garbage.
An array decays to a pointer when passed to a function.
Traverse with for or range-for.

logic.problem: Find the maximum of an array.
logic.thinking: Keep one answer and improve it while scanning.
logic.logic: Compare each element with the best so far.
logic.approach:
1. best = a[0].
2. Scan from index 1.
3. Update best.
logic.code:
int best = a[0];
for (int i = 1; i < n; i++) best = max(best, a[i]);

problems.title: Find Numbers with Even Number of Digits

lessons.title: 012. 2D Arrays
lessons.notes:
int g[r][c]; g[i][j] = row i, column j.
Row-major traversal is cache friendly.
vector<vector<int>> g(r, vector<int>(c, 0));
Directions: dx[] = {1,-1,0,0}, dy[] = {0,0,1,-1}.

logic.problem: Transpose a matrix.
logic.thinking: Cell (i, j) moves to (j, i).
logic.logic: Write the rule for where each cell goes.
logic.approach:
1. Make the result c x r.
2. res[j][i] = g[i][j].
logic.code:
for (int i = 0; i < r; i++)
  for (int j = 0; j < c; j++) res[j][i] = g[i][j];

lessons.title: 013. Strings
lessons.notes:
string s; s.size(), s[i], s + t, substr(pos, len), find, push_back.
Compare with ==, sort with sort(s.begin(), s.end()).
Strings are mutable in C++.
c - 'a' maps letters to 0..25.

logic.problem: Count each letter in a string.
logic.thinking: 26 letters fit in a small array.
logic.logic: Map each letter to an index.
logic.approach:
1. int cnt[26] = {}.
2. cnt[c - 'a']++ for each c.
logic.code:
int cnt[26] = {};
for (char c : s) cnt[c - 'a']++;

problems.title: First Unique Character in a String

lessons.title: 014. Number Problems
lessons.notes:
Last digit: n % 10. Remove last digit: n / 10.
Reverse, palindrome, Armstrong, digit sum.
Watch for overflow when reversing.

logic.problem: Reverse the digits of a number.
logic.thinking: Peel digits from the right, build from the left.
logic.logic: rev = rev * 10 + (n % 10), then n /= 10.
logic.approach:
1. rev = 0.
2. While n > 0 take the last digit.
3. Append it to rev.
logic.code:
long long rev = 0;
while (n > 0) { rev = rev * 10 + n % 10; n /= 10; }

lessons.title: 015. Time Complexity and Big-O
lessons.notes:
Count how steps grow with n, ignore constants.
O(1) < O(log n) < O(n) < O(n log n) < O(n^2) < O(2^n) < O(n!).
About 1e8 simple operations fit in 1 second.
n ≤ 1e5 → O(n log n); n ≤ 1e3 → O(n^2); n ≤ 20 → O(2^n).

logic.problem: Which solution is fast enough for n = 1e5?
logic.thinking: Constraints tell you the allowed complexity.
logic.logic: Match n to the table above.
logic.approach:
1. Read n.
2. Pick the allowed Big-O.
3. Choose an algorithm that fits.
logic.code: // Brute force O(n^2), sort O(n log n), hash set O(n)

lessons.title: 016. Space Complexity
lessons.notes:
Extra memory your algorithm uses.
Recursion uses stack space: depth d means O(d).
Memory limit: about 256 MB ≈ 6e7 ints.
In-place means O(1) extra space.

logic.problem: Trade memory for speed.
logic.thinking: A hash table can turn O(n^2) time into O(n) time at O(n) space.
logic.logic: Spend memory to save time.
logic.approach:
1. Find repeated work.
2. Store its result.
3. Reuse it.

lessons.title: 017. Recursion Basics
lessons.notes:
A function that calls itself on a smaller input.
Always have a base case.
Each call adds a frame on the call stack.
Too deep recursion causes stack overflow (about 1e5 depth).

logic.problem: Find the sum of 1..n.
logic.thinking: sum(n) depends on sum(n-1).
logic.logic: sum(n) = n + sum(n-1), sum(0) = 0.
logic.approach:
1. Write the base case.
2. Reduce n.
3. Combine.
logic.code: int sum(int n) { return n == 0 ? 0 : n + sum(n - 1); }

lessons.title: 018. Recursion Practice and Dry Run
lessons.notes:
Dry run = draw the call tree with arguments and returns.
Count calls to find the complexity: naive fib(n) is O(2^n).
Pass state as parameters instead of globals.

logic.problem: Compute a^n in O(log n).
logic.thinking: a^n = (a^(n/2))^2, halve the problem.
logic.logic: Solve half, square, fix odd.
logic.approach:
1. n == 0 → 1.
2. h = pw(a, n/2).
3. Return h*h (times a if odd).

problems.title: Sum of All Subset Xor Totals

lessons.title: 019. STL: vector
lessons.notes:
vector<int> v; push_back, pop_back, size, back, clear, insert, erase.
push_back is amortised O(1); insert/erase in the middle is O(n).
reserve(n) avoids reallocations.
2D: vector<vector<int>>.

logic.problem: Store n numbers when n is unknown at compile time.
logic.thinking: Arrays are fixed size, vectors grow.
logic.logic: Use vector as the default array.
logic.approach:
1. Declare vector<int> v(n).
2. Fill it, then use it.
logic.code:
vector<int> v(n);
for (int& x : v) cin >> x;

lessons.title: 020. STL: pair, tuple and array
lessons.notes:
pair<int,int> p = {a, b}; p.first, p.second.
Pairs compare by first, then second.
tuple<int,int,int> and get<0>(t).
array<int, 5> is a fixed-size safe array.

logic.problem: Sort people by height but keep their names.
logic.thinking: Keep related values together.
logic.logic: Sort pairs, the key goes first.
logic.approach:
1. Make pair(height, name).
2. sort.
3. Read back.
logic.code:
vector<pair<int,string>> v;
sort(v.rbegin(), v.rend());

problems.title: K Weakest Rows in a Matrix

lessons.title: 021. STL: set, multiset, unordered_set
lessons.notes:
set: sorted, unique, O(log n). unordered_set: O(1) average.
multiset allows duplicates.
insert, erase, find, count, lower_bound.
Use set when you need order, unordered_set when you only need membership.

logic.problem: Do I have this number already?
logic.thinking: Membership checks should be O(1).
logic.logic: Put everything in a set, then ask.
logic.approach:
1. Insert all numbers.
2. For each x, test x-1 and x+1.
logic.code:
unordered_set<int> s(a.begin(), a.end());
bool has = s.count(5);

lessons.title: 022. STL: map and unordered_map
lessons.notes:
map: sorted by key, O(log n). unordered_map: O(1) average.
m[key]++ creates the key with 0 if missing.
for (auto& [k, v] : m)
Use find() when you must not create keys.

logic.problem: Find two numbers adding to target.
logic.thinking: For x, I need to know if target - x was seen.
logic.logic: Store value → index while scanning.
logic.approach:
1. For each x, look up target - x.
2. If found, answer.
3. Else store x.

lessons.title: 023. STL: stack, queue and deque
lessons.notes:
stack: push, pop, top, empty (LIFO).
queue: push, pop, front, back (FIFO).
deque: push/pop at both ends, O(1).
top()/front() on empty is undefined: check empty() first.

logic.problem: Which structure gives the latest or the oldest item?
logic.thinking: Last in first out → stack. First in first out → queue.
logic.logic: Match the access order of the problem.
logic.approach:
1. Write who must leave first.
2. Pick stack or queue.
logic.code: stack<int> st; st.push(1); st.pop();

lessons.title: 024. STL: priority_queue
lessons.notes:
Max-heap by default; min-heap: priority_queue<int, vector<int>, greater<int>>.
push, pop O(log n), top O(1).
Pairs compare by the first element.
No iteration and no random access.

logic.problem: Repeatedly take the largest item.
logic.thinking: Sorting every time is wasteful.
logic.logic: A heap keeps the best item on top.
logic.approach:
1. Push all.
2. Pop the top as needed.
3. Push results back.
logic.code: priority_queue<int, vector<int>, greater<int>> pq;

problems.title: Kth Largest Element in a Stream

lessons.title: 025. STL Algorithms and Comparators
lessons.notes:
sort, reverse, max_element, min_element, accumulate, count, find, unique.
binary_search, lower_bound (≥ x), upper_bound (> x) on sorted data.
Custom sort: lambda [](auto& a, auto& b){ return a.x < b.x; }.
next_permutation walks all permutations.

logic.problem: Sort intervals by start.
logic.thinking: Sorting gives order, then one scan decides.
logic.logic: Choose the key that makes the problem simple.
logic.approach:
1. Sort by key.
2. Scan once.
logic.code: sort(v.begin(), v.end(), [](auto& a, auto& b) { return a[0] < b[0]; });

lessons.title: 026. Iterators and Common Pitfalls
lessons.notes:
Iterator = pointer-like handle: begin(), end().
Erasing or inserting in a vector can invalidate iterators.
v.size() is unsigned: v.size() - 1 on an empty vector gives a huge number.
Use auto and range-for for clean code.

logic.problem: Why does my loop crash on an empty vector?
logic.thinking: Unsigned arithmetic wraps around.
logic.logic: Cast to int when subtracting from size().
logic.approach:
1. int n = v.size().
2. Loop with n - 1.
logic.code: int n = (int)v.size();

lessons.title: 027. Array Basics Problems
lessons.notes:
Max / min / second largest in one pass.
Reverse in place with two indexes.
Rotate: reverse the whole, then reverse the parts.
Always test n = 0, 1, 2.

logic.problem: Rotate an array right by k.
logic.thinking: Reversing three times moves elements without extra memory.
logic.logic: Reverse all, reverse the first k, reverse the rest.
logic.approach:
1. k %= n.
2. reverse the whole array.
3. reverse the first k, then the rest.

problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock

lessons.title: 028. Prefix Sum
lessons.notes:
pre[i] = a[0] + ... + a[i-1].
Range sum [l, r] = pre[r+1] - pre[l] in O(1).
Difference array: add to a range in O(1), rebuild in O(n).
2D prefix sums for rectangles.

logic.problem: Answer many range-sum queries fast.
logic.thinking: Repeated sums repeat work.
logic.logic: Pre-compute once, answer in O(1).
logic.approach:
1. Build pre.
2. Answer = pre[r+1] - pre[l].
logic.code:
vector<long long> pre(n + 1, 0);
for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) pre[i + 1] = pre[i] + a[i];

lessons.title: 029. Kadane's Algorithm
lessons.notes:
Maximum sum of a contiguous subarray in O(n).
At each index: extend the previous subarray, or start fresh.
Works with all-negative arrays if best starts at a[0].
Track indexes to print the subarray.

logic.problem: Maximum sum subarray.
logic.thinking: A negative running sum only hurts the next elements.
logic.logic: cur = max(a[i], cur + a[i]).
logic.approach:
1. cur = best = a[0].
2. Update cur.
3. Update best.

lessons.title: 030. Two Pointers
lessons.notes:
Pointers from both ends (sorted data) or two speeds in one direction.
Used for pair sum, remove duplicates, partition, merge.
Sort first when order does not matter.
O(n) after sorting.

logic.problem: Find a pair with a given sum in a sorted array.
logic.thinking: Checking all pairs is O(n^2). Sorted order tells which pointer to move.
logic.logic: Sum too small → move left; too big → move right.
logic.approach:
1. l = 0, r = n-1.
2. Compare the sum with target.
3. Move one pointer.

problems.title: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted

lessons.title: 031. Sliding Window: Fixed Size
lessons.notes:
Window of exactly k elements.
Add the new element, remove the one that left.
Replaces O(n·k) with O(n).

logic.problem: Maximum sum of k consecutive elements.
logic.thinking: Neighbouring windows share k-1 elements.
logic.logic: sum += a[i] - a[i-k].
logic.approach:
1. Sum the first k.
2. Slide one step at a time.
3. Track the best.
logic.code:
long long s = accumulate(a.begin(), a.begin() + k, 0LL), best = s;
for (int i = k; i < n; i++) { s += a[i] - a[i - k]; best = max(best, s); }

lessons.title: 032. Sliding Window: Variable Size
lessons.notes:
Grow right, shrink left while the window is invalid.
Use it for "longest/shortest subarray with a condition".
Track state in a map or counter.
Each element enters and leaves once: O(n).

logic.problem: Longest substring without repeating letters.
logic.thinking: Brute force checks all substrings; windows share most letters.
logic.logic: If invalid, move left until valid.
logic.approach:
1. Move r, add s[r].
2. While repeated, move l.
3. Update the max length.

lessons.title: 033. Hashing: Frequency Counting
lessons.notes:
Count with unordered_map or an array of size 26 / 256.
Patterns: majority, anagram, top-k, first unique.
Anti-hash tests can slow unordered_map; use map or a custom hash in contests.

logic.problem: Find the element that appears more than n/2 times.
logic.thinking: Counting works, but there is also a voting trick.
logic.logic: Count everything, then read the answer.
logic.approach:
1. cnt[x]++ for each x.
2. Pick the key with the largest count.
logic.code:
unordered_map<int,int> cnt;
for (int x : a) cnt[x]++;

lessons.title: 034. Subarray Sum with Hashing
lessons.notes:
If pre[j] - pre[i] = k then the subarray (i, j] sums to k.
Store how often each prefix sum has occurred.
Seed with {0: 1} for subarrays starting at index 0.
Works with negatives, unlike sliding window.

logic.problem: Count subarrays with sum k.
logic.thinking: Sliding window fails with negatives.
logic.logic: Look for pre - k among earlier prefixes.
logic.approach:
1. map[0] = 1.
2. pre += x.
3. ans += map[pre - k]; map[pre]++.

lessons.title: 035. Elementary Sorting
lessons.notes:
Bubble: swap neighbours, O(n^2).
Selection: pick the minimum, O(n^2).
Insertion: grow a sorted prefix; fast on nearly sorted data.
Know them to understand stability and swaps; use std::sort in practice.

logic.problem: Sort a small array by hand.
logic.thinking: Insert each item into the sorted left part.
logic.logic: Shift larger items right, then place the key.
logic.approach:
1. key = a[i].
2. Shift while a[j] > key.
3. Place key.

lessons.title: 036. Merge Sort
lessons.notes:
Divide into halves, sort, merge. Always O(n log n), stable, O(n) space.
Merge two sorted arrays with two pointers.
The merge step can also count inversions.
Foundation for "count smaller after self".

logic.problem: Sort in guaranteed O(n log n).
logic.thinking: Sorting two halves is easier than the whole.
logic.logic: Merge two sorted halves.
logic.approach:
1. Split at mid.
2. Sort both halves.
3. Merge with two pointers.

problems.title: Count of Smaller Numbers After Self

lessons.title: 037. Quick Sort and Quick Select
lessons.notes:
Pick a pivot, partition, recurse. Average O(n log n), worst O(n^2).
A random pivot avoids the worst case.
Quick select finds the k-th element in O(n) average.

logic.problem: Find the k-th largest without sorting everything.
logic.thinking: Partition tells the final position of the pivot.
logic.logic: Recurse only into the side holding the answer.
logic.approach:
1. Choose a random pivot.
2. Partition around it.
3. Go left or right.
logic.code: nth_element(a.begin(), a.begin() + k, a.end());

problems.title: Kth Largest Element in An Array

lessons.title: 038. Counting Sort and Heap Sort
lessons.notes:
Counting sort: O(n + range) for small integer ranges.
Heap sort: build a heap, pop repeatedly, O(n log n), O(1) extra space.
Radix sort extends counting sort to big numbers.

logic.problem: Sort numbers between 0 and 1000 fast.
logic.thinking: A small range allows direct counting.
logic.logic: Count each value, then rewrite in order.
logic.approach:
1. cnt[x]++.
2. Output each value cnt times.
logic.code:
vector<int> cnt(1001);
for (int x : a) cnt[x]++;

lessons.title: 039. Dutch National Flag and Partitioning
lessons.notes:
Three-way partition with three pointers: low, mid, high.
Sort 0/1/2 in one pass, O(1) space.
Same idea as the quick sort partition.

logic.problem: Sort an array of 0s, 1s and 2s.
logic.thinking: Only three values exist; a single pass can place them.
logic.logic: 0 goes left, 2 goes right, 1 stays.
logic.approach:
1. lo = mid = 0, hi = n-1.
2. Swap by the value of a[mid].

lessons.title: 040. Matrix Problems
lessons.notes:
Spiral: four boundaries top, bottom, left, right.
Rotate 90°: transpose, then reverse each row.
Search a sorted matrix from the top-right corner in O(r + c).
Mark zeros using the first row and column for O(1) space.

logic.problem: Rotate an n×n matrix by 90°.
logic.thinking: Rotation = transpose + mirror.
logic.logic: Break a hard move into two easy ones.
logic.approach:
1. Transpose.
2. Reverse every row.
logic.code:
for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) for (int j = i + 1; j < n; j++) swap(g[i][j], g[j][i]);
for (auto& row : g) reverse(row.begin(), row.end());

lessons.title: 041. String Problems
lessons.notes:
Palindrome check with two pointers.
Anagram: compare sorted strings or counts.
Reverse words: split, reverse, join.
Longest palindromic substring: expand around each centre in O(n^2).

logic.problem: Longest palindromic substring.
logic.thinking: Every palindrome has a centre.
logic.logic: Try each centre and grow outwards.
logic.approach:
1. For each i, try odd and even centres.
2. Expand while equal.
3. Track the longest.

lessons.title: 042. KMP and Rabin-Karp
lessons.notes:
KMP: the LPS array stores the longest proper prefix that is also a suffix.
Search in O(n + m) without going back in the text.
Rabin-Karp: rolling hash of the window, compare hashes first.
Use a modulus and verify matches to avoid collisions.

logic.problem: Find a pattern in a text quickly.
logic.thinking: After a mismatch, part of the pattern is already matched.
logic.logic: Reuse matched prefixes using LPS.
logic.approach:
1. Build LPS.
2. Walk text and pattern.
3. On mismatch jump j = lps[j-1].

problems.title: Find the Index of the First Occurrence in a String

lessons.title: 043. Binary Search Basics
lessons.notes:
Needs sorted or monotonic data, O(log n).
Use mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2 to avoid overflow.
Decide: closed [lo, hi] or half-open [lo, hi).
Loop invariant: the answer is always inside [lo, hi].

logic.problem: Find x in a sorted array.
logic.thinking: Each check removes half of the candidates.
logic.logic: Compare mid, discard half.
logic.approach:
1. lo = 0, hi = n-1.
2. Take mid and compare.
3. Shrink.

lessons.title: 044. Binary Search Variations
lessons.notes:
First occurrence = lower_bound; last = upper_bound - 1.
Count of x = upper_bound - lower_bound.
Floor and ceil of x.
Do not stop when you find x: keep searching one side.

logic.problem: First position where a[i] >= x.
logic.thinking: Answers go no, no, yes, yes.
logic.logic: If mid is good, keep it and go left.
logic.approach:
1. lo = 0, hi = n.
2. If a[mid] >= x, hi = mid, else lo = mid + 1.
3. Answer is lo.

problems.title: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array

lessons.title: 045. Binary Search on Rotated Arrays
lessons.notes:
One half of a rotated sorted array is always sorted.
Decide which half is sorted, then check if x is inside it.
Minimum element: compare a[mid] with a[hi].
Duplicates may need a linear step.

logic.problem: Search in a rotated sorted array.
logic.thinking: Sorted half = reliable half.
logic.logic: Test the sorted half first.
logic.approach:
1. Find the sorted half.
2. If x is in it, go there.
3. Else go to the other half.

lessons.title: 046. Binary Search on Answer
lessons.notes:
Search the answer range, not the array.
Needs a monotonic yes/no check: if X works, a bigger X also works.
Template: feasible(mid) ? hi = mid : lo = mid + 1.
Examples: Koko bananas, ship packages, split array.

logic.problem: Smallest eating speed that finishes in h hours.
logic.thinking: Higher speed never hurts, so answers go no, no, yes, yes.
logic.logic: Write feasible(x), then search.
logic.approach:
1. Set lo and hi.
2. Test mid.
3. Shrink toward the smallest feasible value.

problems.title: Capacity to Ship Packages Within D Days

lessons.title: 047. Linked List Basics
lessons.notes:
struct Node { int val; Node* next; };
Insert at head O(1); at tail O(n) without a tail pointer.
Delete: link the previous node to the next one.
Use a dummy head to avoid special cases.

logic.problem: Remove all nodes with value x.
logic.thinking: Deleting the head is a special case.
logic.logic: A dummy before head makes all deletions alike.
logic.approach:
1. dummy->next = head.
2. Walk with a pointer.
3. Skip nodes equal to x.

problems.title: Delete Node in a Linked List

lessons.title: 048. Reverse a Linked List
lessons.notes:
Iterative: prev, cur, next.
Recursive: reverse the rest, then fix the head.
Reverse a part [l, r], or in groups of k.
Always save next before changing it.

logic.problem: Reverse a list.
logic.thinking: Every pointer must point backwards.
logic.logic: Save next, flip, move on.
logic.approach:
1. prev = null.
2. nxt = cur->next.
3. cur->next = prev, then advance.

lessons.title: 049. Fast and Slow Pointers
lessons.notes:
Slow moves 1 step, fast moves 2.
Middle: when fast ends, slow is in the middle.
Cycle: if they meet, there is a cycle.
Cycle start: reset one pointer to head, move both by 1.

logic.problem: Detect a cycle without extra memory.
logic.thinking: A faster runner eventually laps a slower one.
logic.logic: The pointers meet only inside a cycle.
logic.approach:
1. slow = fast = head.
2. Move by 1 and 2.
3. If equal, there is a cycle.

lessons.title: 050. Merge and Sort Linked Lists
lessons.notes:
Merge two sorted lists with a dummy node.
Sort a list: split with slow/fast, sort halves, merge, O(n log n).
Merge sort suits lists because no random access is needed.

logic.problem: Merge two sorted lists.
logic.thinking: Always attach the smaller head.
logic.logic: Compare heads, append the smaller.
logic.approach:
1. dummy and tail.
2. Compare a and b.
3. Attach the rest.

lessons.title: 051. Doubly and Circular Linked Lists
lessons.notes:
Doubly: prev and next pointers; delete a node in O(1) if you hold it.
Circular: tail->next = head.
Careful with four pointer updates on insert.
std::list is a doubly linked list.

logic.problem: Insert a node after a given node in a doubly list.
logic.thinking: Four links change.
logic.logic: Update the new node first, then the neighbours.
logic.approach:
1. n->next = p->next; n->prev = p.
2. If p->next, p->next->prev = n.
3. p->next = n.

problems.title: Flatten a Multilevel Doubly Linked List

lessons.title: 052. Linked List Interview Problems
lessons.notes:
Remove n-th from end: two pointers n apart.
Intersection: switch heads when you reach the end.
Palindrome list: find the middle, reverse the half, compare.
LRU cache: hash map + doubly linked list, O(1) get and put.

logic.problem: Design an LRU cache.
logic.thinking: Need O(1) lookup and O(1) reorder.
logic.logic: The map gives the node, the list gives the order.
logic.approach:
1. Map key → list iterator.
2. On use, move to front.
3. On overflow, erase the back.
logic.code:
list<pair<int,int>> dq;
unordered_map<int, list<pair<int,int>>::iterator> mp;

problems.title: Remove Nth Node from End of List

lessons.title: 053. Stack and Its Applications
lessons.notes:
Stack = last in, first out; all operations O(1).
Use cases: undo, brackets, DFS, recursion.
Implement with a vector or array and a top index.
Check empty() before top().

logic.problem: Check if brackets are balanced.
logic.thinking: The latest opener must close first.
logic.logic: A closer must match the top.
logic.approach:
1. Push openers.
2. On a closer, compare with top and pop.
3. The stack must end empty.

problems.title: Remove All Adjacent Duplicates in String

lessons.title: 054. Monotonic Stack
lessons.notes:
Keep the stack increasing or decreasing.
Next greater / smaller element in O(n): each item is pushed and popped once.
Store indexes to compute distances.
Used in histogram, stock span, trapping water.

logic.problem: Days until a warmer temperature.
logic.thinking: Compare each day with unresolved earlier days.
logic.logic: Pop days that just found their answer.
logic.approach:
1. Stack of indexes with decreasing temperatures.
2. While today > top, pop and fill the answer.
3. Push today.

lessons.title: 055. Expression Evaluation
lessons.notes:
Postfix (RPN): push numbers, apply an operator to the top two.
Infix to postfix: operator stack and precedence.
Calculator: one stack for numbers and a sign.
Mind the operand order for - and /.

logic.problem: Evaluate a postfix expression.
logic.thinking: An operator always acts on the last two numbers.
logic.logic: Pop b, then a, compute a op b.
logic.approach:
1. Read a token.
2. Number → push.
3. Operator → pop two, push the result.

lessons.title: 056. Queue and Circular Queue
lessons.notes:
Queue = first in, first out.
Circular queue: use (i + 1) % size to reuse space.
Full vs empty: track the count.
BFS is built on a queue.

logic.problem: Implement a fixed-size queue.
logic.thinking: A plain array wastes slots after pops.
logic.logic: Wrap indexes with modulo.
logic.approach:
1. head, tail, count.
2. push: arr[tail] = x; tail = (tail+1)%k.
3. pop: head = (head+1)%k.

lessons.title: 057. Monotonic Deque
lessons.notes:
The deque keeps indexes with decreasing values.
Front = maximum of the current window.
Remove from the front if out of the window, from the back if smaller.
O(n) overall.

logic.problem: Maximum in every window of size k.
logic.thinking: Smaller items before a bigger one can never be the maximum.
logic.logic: Keep only useful candidates.
logic.approach:
1. Pop back while smaller.
2. Push i.
3. Pop front if outside.
4. The front is the answer.

problems.title: Shortest Subarray with Sum at Least K

lessons.title: 058. Stack and Queue Design Problems
lessons.notes:
Min stack: store (value, minSoFar).
Queue using two stacks: move items when the out-stack is empty.
Stack using queues: rotate after each push.
Amortised O(1).

logic.problem: Get the minimum of a stack in O(1).
logic.thinking: Each state needs to remember its own minimum.
logic.logic: Push the pair (x, min).
logic.approach:
1. st.push({x, min(x, st.top().second)}).
2. getMin = top.second.
logic.code: stack<pair<int,int>> st;

lessons.title: 059. Subsets and Subsequences
lessons.notes:
n items → 2^n subsets.
Pick or skip each item.
For duplicates: sort, skip equal items at the same level.
Same idea for subsequences.

logic.problem: List all subsets.
logic.thinking: Every item has two choices: take or skip.
logic.logic: Choose, recurse, undo.
logic.approach:
1. If i == n, store the path.
2. Take a[i], recurse.
3. Undo, skip, recurse.

lessons.title: 060. Permutations
lessons.notes:
n! arrangements.
Use a used[] array, or swap elements in place.
Duplicates: sort and skip repeats at the same level.
next_permutation is a shortcut for sorted input.

logic.problem: List all permutations.
logic.thinking: Each position takes any unused item.
logic.logic: Pick an unused element for the next slot.
logic.approach:
1. If the path is full, store it.
2. Try each unused item.
3. Undo.

lessons.title: 061. Combination Sum
lessons.notes:
Start the loop from the current index to avoid duplicates.
Reuse allowed: recurse with the same index. Not allowed: i + 1.
Prune when the remaining sum < 0.
Sort to skip equal items.

logic.problem: Find all combinations that add to a target.
logic.thinking: Order should not matter, so move forward only.
logic.logic: Loop from start and prune.
logic.approach:
1. If rem == 0, store.
2. For i from start, take a[i].
3. Recurse and undo.

lessons.title: 062. N-Queens
lessons.notes:
Place one queen per row.
Track columns and both diagonals: r - c and r + c.
Pruning makes it practical for n up to 12.
The same idea solves Sudoku.

logic.problem: Place n queens so none attack each other.
logic.thinking: Only one queen per row is possible.
logic.logic: Check column and diagonals in O(1).
logic.approach:
1. Go row by row.
2. Try each free column.
3. Mark, recurse, unmark.

lessons.title: 063. Grid and String Backtracking
lessons.notes:
Word search: DFS in 4 directions, mark visited, unmark on return.
Palindrome partitioning: cut at every position that forms a palindrome.
Generate parentheses: add "(" if open < n, ")" if close < open.
Always undo the change.

logic.problem: Does a word exist in a grid?
logic.thinking: Try every start cell and follow matching neighbours.
logic.logic: Mark the cell, explore, restore it.
logic.approach:
1. Match the current letter.
2. Mark visited.
3. Try four directions.
4. Restore.

lessons.title: 064. Binary Tree Basics and Traversals
lessons.notes:
struct TreeNode { int val; TreeNode *left, *right; };
Preorder: root, left, right. Inorder: left, root, right. Postorder: left, right, root.
Recursion depth = tree height.
A skewed tree has height n.

logic.problem: Visit all nodes of a BST in sorted order.
logic.thinking: Inorder visits left, then the node, then right.
logic.logic: Pick the order that matches the question.
logic.approach:
1. Base case: null returns.
2. Recurse left.
3. Visit.
4. Recurse right.

lessons.title: 065. Iterative Tree Traversals
lessons.notes:
Use your own stack to avoid recursion depth limits.
Inorder: go left as far as possible, pop, visit, go right.
Preorder: push right then left.
Postorder: reverse of (root, right, left).

logic.problem: Do an inorder traversal without recursion.
logic.thinking: The call stack can be replaced by an explicit stack.
logic.logic: Go left, pop, go right.
logic.approach:
1. Push the left chain.
2. Pop and visit.
3. Move to the right child.

lessons.title: 066. Level Order and Tree Views
lessons.notes:
BFS with a queue; process level by level using the queue size.
Right view: last node of each level.
Zigzag: reverse alternate levels.
Vertical order: BFS with a column index.

logic.problem: Print nodes level by level.
logic.thinking: Nodes at the same depth are visited together.
logic.logic: Freeze the queue size for each level.
logic.approach:
1. Push the root.
2. n = q.size().
3. Process n nodes, push their children.

problems.title: Binary Tree Zigzag Level Order Traversal

lessons.title: 067. Tree Recursion Problems
lessons.notes:
Most tree answers combine the left answer and the right answer.
Height, diameter, balanced check, invert, symmetric.
Return one value, update a global for the other.
Complexity is usually O(n).

logic.problem: Diameter of a binary tree.
logic.thinking: The longest path bends at some node.
logic.logic: At each node: best = left height + right height.
logic.approach:
1. Get heights from the children.
2. Update the answer.
3. Return 1 + max.

lessons.title: 068. LCA and Path Problems
lessons.notes:
LCA: if left and right both return a node, the current node is the LCA.
Path sum: subtract while moving down.
Max path sum: the best path may bend; return the better single side.
Root-to-leaf paths use backtracking.

logic.problem: Find the lowest common ancestor of p and q.
logic.thinking: It is the first node that sees p on one side and q on the other.
logic.logic: Return the node when it is p or q.
logic.approach:
1. Null, p or q → return the node.
2. Search both sides.
3. Both non-null → this node.

problems.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree

lessons.title: 069. Construct Tree from Traversals
lessons.notes:
Preorder gives the root first; inorder splits left and right.
Postorder gives the root last.
Use a map from value to inorder index for O(n).
Preorder + postorder alone cannot give a unique tree.

logic.problem: Rebuild a tree from preorder and inorder.
logic.thinking: The first preorder item is the root.
logic.logic: Find the root in inorder; the left part is the left subtree.
logic.approach:
1. root = pre[i++].
2. Find root in inorder.
3. Build left, then right.

lessons.title: 070. BST Basics
lessons.notes:
Left < node < right, and inorder is sorted.
Search and insert take O(h); delete has three cases.
Delete: leaf, one child, or two children (replace with the inorder successor).
Balanced height is log n; skewed is n.

logic.problem: Insert a value into a BST.
logic.thinking: Walk left or right until you find a null spot.
logic.logic: Smaller goes left, larger goes right.
logic.approach:
1. If null, create a node.
2. Compare and recurse.
3. Return the root.

problems.title: Search in a Binary Search Tree
Insert Into a Binary Search Tree

lessons.title: 071. BST Problems
lessons.notes:
Validate with a (low, high) range for each node.
k-th smallest: inorder traversal and count.
LCA in a BST: go left or right by value.
Floor, ceil, successor, predecessor.

logic.problem: Check if a tree is a BST.
logic.thinking: Comparing only with the parent is not enough.
logic.logic: Pass the allowed range down.
logic.approach:
1. Start with (-inf, +inf).
2. Left child: update high.
3. Right child: update low.

problems.title: Kth Smallest Element in a Bst
Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree

lessons.title: 072. Segment Tree
lessons.notes:
Answers range queries and point updates in O(log n).
Store the answer of each segment (sum, min, max).
Size 4n array; node i has children 2i and 2i+1.
Lazy propagation handles range updates.

logic.problem: Many range-sum queries with updates.
logic.thinking: Prefix sums break when values change.
logic.logic: Split into halves, store each half's answer.
logic.approach:
1. Build recursively.
2. Query: combine overlapping segments.
3. Update: change a leaf, recompute parents.

lessons.title: 073. Fenwick Tree (BIT)
lessons.notes:
Shorter than a segment tree for prefix sums.
i & -i is the lowest set bit.
update(i, d): i += i & -i. query(i): i -= i & -i.
1-indexed; O(log n).

logic.problem: Count items smaller than x seen so far.
logic.thinking: You need prefix counts that change over time.
logic.logic: Each cell stores a block of the prefix.
logic.approach:
1. Compress the values.
2. Query the count, then update.
logic.code:
void upd(int i, int d) { for (; i <= n; i += i & -i) bit[i] += d; }
int qry(int i) { int s = 0; for (; i > 0; i -= i & -i) s += bit[i]; return s; }

problems.title: Count of Smaller Numbers After Self

lessons.title: 074. Trie
lessons.notes:
A tree of characters; each path = a prefix.
Insert, search and prefix search in O(word length).
Node: array of 26 children + end flag.
Great for autocomplete and word games.

logic.problem: Check if a word or prefix exists.
logic.thinking: A hash set cannot answer prefix questions quickly.
logic.logic: Share common prefixes.
logic.approach:
1. Walk letter by letter.
2. Create missing nodes on insert.
3. Mark the end.

problems.title: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure

lessons.title: 075. Tree Design: Serialize and Recover
lessons.notes:
Serialize with preorder and null markers.
Deserialize by reading tokens in the same order.
Recover a BST: the inorder has two swapped values.
Morris traversal gives O(1) space traversal.

logic.problem: Turn a tree into a string and back.
logic.thinking: Null markers keep the shape.
logic.logic: The same order writes and reads.
logic.approach:
1. Write val or "#".
2. Recurse left, then right.
3. Read in the same order.

lessons.title: 076. Heap Internals
lessons.notes:
A complete binary tree stored in an array.
Parent (i-1)/2, children 2i+1 and 2i+2.
Push: add at the end, sift up. Pop: move the last to the root, sift down.
Build a heap in O(n) with heapify.

logic.problem: Get the minimum repeatedly.
logic.thinking: A heap gives the min in O(1) and updates in O(log n).
logic.logic: Keep the heap property after each change.
logic.approach:
1. Push at the end.
2. Sift up.
3. For pop, sift down.

problems.title: Kth Smallest Element in a Sorted Matrix

lessons.title: 077. Top K Problems
lessons.notes:
Top K largest: keep a min-heap of size K.
Top K frequent: count, then heap.
O(n log k) is better than sorting O(n log n).
Or use quick select for O(n) average.

logic.problem: K closest points to the origin.
logic.thinking: You only need K items, not a full order.
logic.logic: Keep the K best; kick out the worst.
logic.approach:
1. Push each item.
2. If size > K, pop.
3. The heap holds the answer.

lessons.title: 078. Merge K Lists and Median Stream
lessons.notes:
Merge K sorted lists with a min-heap of heads: O(N log K).
Median of a stream: max-heap for the lower half, min-heap for the upper half.
Keep sizes equal or off by one.
Task scheduling: greedy with a heap.

logic.problem: Running median of a stream.
logic.thinking: Sorting after every insert is too slow.
logic.logic: The tops of two heaps hold the middle.
logic.approach:
1. Push into low.
2. Move the low top to high.
3. Rebalance the sizes.

lessons.title: 079. Graph Representation
lessons.notes:
Adjacency list: vector<int> g[n]; O(V + E) memory.
Adjacency matrix: O(V^2) memory, O(1) edge check.
Weighted: vector<pair<int,int>> g[n].
Directed vs undirected: add one or two edges.

logic.problem: Store a graph with n nodes and m edges.
logic.thinking: Most graphs are sparse.
logic.logic: Store only the neighbours.
logic.approach:
1. Read edges.
2. g[u].push_back(v).
3. For undirected, also g[v].push_back(u).
logic.code:
vector<vector<int>> g(n);
for (auto& e : edges) { g[e[0]].push_back(e[1]); g[e[1]].push_back(e[0]); }

lessons.title: 080. BFS
lessons.notes:
BFS visits nodes level by level using a queue.
Gives the shortest path in unweighted graphs.
Mark visited when you push, not when you pop.
Grid BFS: four directions, bounds check.

logic.problem: Shortest path in an unweighted graph.
logic.thinking: Every edge has the same cost.
logic.logic: The first time you reach a node is the shortest way.
logic.approach:
1. Push the start, dist = 0.
2. Pop and visit neighbours.
3. dist[v] = dist[u] + 1.

lessons.title: 081. DFS and Connected Components
lessons.notes:
DFS goes deep first; use recursion or a stack.
Count components: start a DFS from each unvisited node.
Grid DFS: flood fill, islands.
Track entry/exit times for later topics.

logic.problem: Count islands in a grid.
logic.thinking: Each island is one connected group.
logic.logic: Visit a land cell, sink all connected cells.
logic.approach:
1. Scan the cells.
2. On land, count + 1 and DFS.
3. DFS marks cells visited.

lessons.title: 082. Cycle Detection
lessons.notes:
Undirected: DFS; if you meet a visited node that is not the parent → cycle.
Directed: track the recursion stack (0 = new, 1 = in progress, 2 = done).
Or use topological sort / DSU.
Course Schedule is a cycle question.

logic.problem: Can all courses be finished?
logic.thinking: Impossible exactly when the prerequisite graph has a cycle.
logic.logic: An edge to an in-progress node is a cycle.
logic.approach:
1. state[u] = 1.
2. If state[v] == 1, cycle.
3. state[u] = 2.

lessons.title: 083. Topological Sort
lessons.notes:
A linear order of a DAG so every edge goes forward.
Kahn's algorithm: BFS using in-degrees.
DFS version: push after finishing, then reverse.
If fewer than n nodes are output, there is a cycle.

logic.problem: Order tasks with dependencies.
logic.thinking: A task can start when all its prerequisites are done.
logic.logic: Take nodes with in-degree 0.
logic.approach:
1. Compute in-degrees.
2. Queue the zero ones.
3. Pop and reduce neighbours.

lessons.title: 084. Dijkstra's Algorithm
lessons.notes:
Shortest paths with non-negative weights.
Min-heap of (distance, node); skip stale entries.
O((V + E) log V).
Not valid with negative edges.

logic.problem: Shortest path in a weighted graph.
logic.thinking: BFS counts edges, but edges now have costs.
logic.logic: Always expand the closest unsettled node.
logic.approach:
1. dist[s] = 0, push.
2. Pop the smallest.
3. Relax each edge.

lessons.title: 085. Bellman-Ford and Floyd-Warshall
lessons.notes:
Bellman-Ford: relax all edges V-1 times; handles negative edges; detects negative cycles. O(VE).
Floyd-Warshall: all pairs, O(V^3).
for k, for i, for j: d[i][j] = min(d[i][j], d[i][k] + d[k][j]).
Use it for small V only.

logic.problem: Shortest path with negative edges.
logic.thinking: Dijkstra fails with negatives.
logic.logic: A shortest path has at most V-1 edges.
logic.approach:
1. dist[s] = 0.
2. Repeat V-1 times: relax every edge.
3. One more round reveals a negative cycle.

problems.title: Find the City with the Smallest Number of Neighbors at a Threshold Distance

lessons.title: 086. Minimum Spanning Tree
lessons.notes:
An MST connects all nodes with minimum total weight.
Kruskal: sort edges, add if it joins different components (DSU).
Prim: grow from a node with a min-heap.
V-1 edges are chosen.

logic.problem: Connect all cities with minimum cable.
logic.thinking: Take cheap edges that do not form a cycle.
logic.logic: Kruskal's algorithm.
logic.approach:
1. Sort the edges.
2. For each edge, if find(u) != find(v), unite.
3. Add the weight.
logic.code:
sort(edges.begin(), edges.end());
for (auto& [w, u, v] : edges) if (unite(u, v)) total += w;

Find Critical and Pseudo Critical Edges in Minimum Spanning Tree

lessons.title: 087. Disjoint Set Union
lessons.notes:
find with path compression, union by size/rank.
Near O(1) per operation.
Use for connected groups, cycle detection in undirected graphs, Kruskal.
Accounts merge, grouping problems.

logic.problem: Are two nodes connected?
logic.thinking: Groups merge over time.
logic.logic: Each group has one representative.
logic.approach:
1. parent[i] = i.
2. find compresses the path.
3. unite attaches the smaller to the bigger.

problems.title: Most Stones Removed with Same Row Or Column

lessons.title: 088. DP Introduction
lessons.notes:
DP = recursion + remembering answers.
Overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure.
Top-down (memoisation) vs bottom-up (tabulation).
Steps: state, transition, base case, order, answer.

logic.problem: Count ways to climb n stairs.
logic.thinking: The last move came from step n-1 or n-2.
logic.logic: ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2).
logic.approach:
1. dp[0] = dp[1] = 1.
2. Fill left to right.
3. The answer is dp[n].
logic.code:
vector<long long> dp(n + 1, 1);
for (int i = 2; i <= n; i++) dp[i] = dp[i - 1] + dp[i - 2];

lessons.title: 089. 1D DP
lessons.notes:
The state depends on a few earlier states.
House robber: take or skip.
Decode ways: one or two characters.
Space-optimise to O(1) with two variables.

logic.problem: Maximum money without robbing neighbours.
logic.thinking: At each house: rob it or skip it.
logic.logic: dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], dp[i-2] + a[i]).
logic.approach:
1. Handle small n.
2. Fill dp.
3. Return dp[n-1].
logic.code:
int prev2 = 0, prev1 = 0;
for (int x : a) { int cur = max(prev1, prev2 + x); prev2 = prev1; prev1 = cur; }

lessons.title: 090. 0/1 Knapsack
lessons.notes:
Each item is used at most once.
dp[i][w] = max(skip, take).
1D version: loop w from high to low.
Subset sum, partition and target sum use the same idea.

logic.problem: Pick items to maximise value within capacity W.
logic.thinking: For each item there are two choices.
logic.logic: dp[w] = max(dp[w], dp[w - wt] + val).
logic.approach:
1. dp[0..W] = 0.
2. For each item, loop w from W down to wt.
3. The answer is dp[W].
logic.code:
for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
  for (int w = W; w >= wt[i]; w--) dp[w] = max(dp[w], dp[w - wt[i]] + val[i]);

lessons.title: 091. Unbounded Knapsack and Coin Change
lessons.notes:
Items can be reused: loop w from low to high.
Coin change (min coins): dp[a] = 1 + min(dp[a - c]).
Coin change II (ways): loop coins outside to count combinations.
Perfect squares is the same pattern.

logic.problem: Minimum coins to make an amount.
logic.thinking: The best answer for a uses the best answer for a smaller amount.
logic.logic: dp[a] = 1 + min(dp[a - c]).
logic.approach:
1. dp[0] = 0, others INF.
2. Fill from 1 to amount.
3. Return -1 if INF.

lessons.title: 092. LCS and String DP
lessons.notes:
LCS: if letters match, 1 + diagonal; else max(up, left).
Edit distance: insert, delete, replace.
Longest palindromic subsequence = LCS(s, reverse(s)).
2D table; roll rows to save space.

logic.problem: Longest common subsequence of two strings.
logic.thinking: Compare the last letters of both strings.
logic.logic: Match → diagonal + 1; else the best of two.
logic.approach:
1. dp[0][*] = dp[*][0] = 0.
2. Fill row by row.
3. The answer is dp[n][m].

lessons.title: 093. Longest Increasing Subsequence
lessons.notes:
O(n^2) DP: dp[i] = 1 + max(dp[j]) for a[j] < a[i].
O(n log n): keep the smallest tail for each length with lower_bound.
Russian doll envelopes: sort, then LIS.
Counting LIS needs an extra counter.

logic.problem: Length of the longest increasing subsequence.
logic.thinking: A smaller tail allows longer extensions.
logic.logic: Replace the first tail ≥ x.
logic.approach:
1. tails = empty.
2. lower_bound for x.
3. Replace or append.

lessons.title: 094. Grid DP
lessons.notes:
dp[i][j] depends on up and left.
Unique paths, minimum path sum, maximal square, triangle.
Handle obstacles and borders.
Rolling row for O(cols) space.

logic.problem: Count paths from top-left to bottom-right.
logic.thinking: You can arrive only from the top or from the left.
logic.approach:
1. First row and column = 1.
2. Fill the rest.
3. The answer is bottom-right.
logic.code:
for (int i = 1; i < m; i++)
  for (int j = 1; j < n; j++) dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j] + dp[i][j - 1];

lessons.title: 095. Advanced DP: Bitmask and Trees
lessons.notes:
Bitmask DP: the mask stores which items are used; n ≤ 20.
Tree DP: combine child answers (house robber III).
State = (node, taken or not).
Write the state clearly before coding.

logic.problem: Rob houses arranged as a tree.
logic.thinking: Robbing a node blocks its children.
logic.logic: Return a pair (take, skip) from each node.
logic.approach:
1. Get pairs from the children.
2. take = val + skip of children.
3. skip = best of children.

problems.title: Partition to K Equal Sum Subsets

lessons.title: 096. Greedy and Intervals
lessons.notes:
Greedy: a local best choice that is provably safe.
Sort first, then scan.
Intervals: sort by start (merge) or by end (maximum non-overlapping).
If you cannot prove it, test against brute force.

logic.problem: Maximum number of non-overlapping intervals.
logic.thinking: Finishing early leaves the most room.
logic.logic: Always keep the interval that ends first.
logic.approach:
1. Sort by end.
2. Take it if start ≥ last end.
3. Count.

problems.title: Minimum Number of Arrows to Burst Balloons

lessons.title: 097. Bit Manipulation
lessons.notes:
& | ^ ~ << >>
Check bit i: (n >> i) & 1. Set: n | (1 << i). Clear: n & ~(1 << i).
n & (n - 1) removes the lowest set bit.
XOR cancels pairs: a ^ a = 0.
__builtin_popcount counts set bits.

logic.problem: Find the number that appears once.
logic.thinking: Pairs cancel under XOR.
logic.logic: XOR everything.
logic.approach:
1. ans = 0.
2. ans ^= x for each x.
3. Return ans.
logic.code:
int ans = 0;
for (int x : a) ans ^= x;

lessons.title: 098. Math and Number Theory
lessons.notes:
gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b); std::gcd in C++17.
Sieve of Eratosthenes: O(n log log n).
Fast power with modulo; mod = 1e9 + 7.
Remember (a * b) % m needs long long.

logic.problem: Compute a^b mod m fast.
logic.thinking: Repeated squaring halves the exponent.
logic.logic: If b is odd, multiply the answer once.
logic.approach:
1. res = 1.
2. If b is odd, res = res * a % m.
3. a = a * a % m; b >>= 1.

lessons.title: 099. Choosing the Right Pattern
lessons.notes:
Sorted array / pair → two pointers or binary search.
Subarray or substring → sliding window or prefix sum.
Next greater → monotonic stack.
Shortest path → BFS or Dijkstra.
All possibilities → backtracking.
Overlapping subproblems → DP.
Top K → heap.

logic.problem: Which technique does this problem need?
logic.thinking: Clues in the statement point to the pattern.
logic.logic: Read the constraints and the wording.
logic.approach:
1. Restate the problem.
2. Match clues to a pattern.
3. State the complexity, then code.

lessons.title: 100. Final Roadmap and Contest Template
lessons.notes:
Practice plan: 1 topic per week, 5 easy, 5 medium, 1 hard.
Always: restate, brute force, optimise, test, state complexity.
Keep a template with fast I/O and common macros.
Revise your mistakes notebook weekly.

logic.problem: Where do I go from here?
logic.thinking: Consistent practice beats long rare sessions.
logic.logic: Review mistakes and re-solve after a week.
logic.approach:
1. Pick a topic.
2. Solve, then review.
3. Re-solve after 7 days.
